claims.text: The Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) is a Visa specification that lets an AI agent prove its identity to a merchant by signing its web requests.
TAP identifies agents; it does not move money by itself.
TAP is not an IETF standard; it is published by Visa on the Visa Developer Center under Visa's own terms.
Visa announced the Trusted Agent Protocol on 2025-10-14.
Visa says TAP was developed in collaboration with Cloudflare.
Visa's launch release names Adyen, Ant International, Checkout.com, Coinbase, CyberSource, Elavon, Fiserv, Microsoft, Nuvei, Shopify, Stripe and Worldpay as early partners that gave feedback.
Visa's TAP overview page, retired in October 2026, presented TAP as an enhancement to Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC).
Visa unveiled Visa Intelligent Commerce on 2025-04-30.

Until at least 2026-10-12 Visa's TAP overview page said the product was in the process of development and deployment and might not be available in all markets; Visa retired that page in October 2026, and the Getting started page that replaced it carries no such note.
Visa's launch release says Visa is committed to aligning with standards bodies such as the IETF, the OpenID Foundation and EMVCo.
Visa's launch release says the initial TAP specifications apply to the Visa network in this phase.
The TAP Product Terms are dated 2025-10-10.
The TAP Product Terms grant a nonexclusive, non-sublicensable, nontransferable and revocable license.
The TAP license is conditioned on implementing the most current version of the specification in its entirety and in strict conformance.

The TAP Product Terms bar modifications to the specification, allow the sample code to be adapted or ported only as needed to build applications that implement the current specification, and assign any unpermitted modification to Visa.
Implementers must apply each Visa update to TAP at least annually and within six months of its publication.
The TAP Product Terms say production use does not require submission to Visa's Solution Approval process.
Under the TAP Product Terms the implementer alone is responsible for disclosures to users and for collecting any consents that law requires.

The repository's LICENSE.md is not an open source license: it binds users to the Visa Developer Center Terms of Use and the TAP Product Terms, while the source files carry MIT-style permission text, and which text governs is not stated.
Source files in the TAP sample repository start with a Visa copyright line followed by MIT-style permission text, which conflicts with the repository's LICENSE.md.
GitHub reports the license of visa/trusted-agent-protocol as unrecognized (NOASSERTION).
The visa/trusted-agent-protocol repository was created on GitHub on 2025-10-10.
The TAP specification page carries no version number and no publication date.
The TAP reference repository has six commits, dated 2025-10-12 to 2025-10-28, and no tags or releases.
The last commit to the TAP reference repository, which added nonce validation sample code, was merged on 2025-10-28.
As of 2026-10-11, no pull request to the TAP reference repository has been merged since 2025-10-28; twelve later pull requests are open or were closed unmerged.
An open pull request opened on 2026-07-15 proposes making the sample merchant signature verifier conform to RFC 9421.
An open issue opened on 2026-07-18 says the signature base for the consumer recognition object and payment container is under-specified and asks for a test vector.
On 2026-10-19 the TAP reference repository had 213 stars and 46 forks on GitHub.
The TAP specification names these participants: Agent Providers, Checkout Enablers, Consumers, Site Protection Providers, Identity Providers, Merchants, Payment Schemes and a Key Store.
In TAP, Agent Providers are certified AI platforms onboarded to payment schemes and approved to pay on behalf of account holders.
The only expectation TAP places on Checkout Enablers is that they pass message signatures and query parameters through to the merchant.
TAP defines Site Protection Providers as layers in front of a merchant site, such as CDNs, trust management systems or proxies.
The TAP specification says merchants are not required to use the protocol and do not necessarily have to be registered with payment schemes to accept their credentials.
Verification of TAP signatures can be done by the merchant itself or by a Site Protection Provider on its behalf.
The TAP sample repository models five services: an agent, a merchant frontend, a merchant backend, a CDN proxy and an agent registry.
TAP's agent recognition signature uses the RFC 9421 Signature-Input and Signature header fields.
The minimum covered components of a TAP message signature are @authority and @path.
A TAP message signature must carry the parameters created, expires, keyid, alg, nonce and tag.
TAP defines two tag values: agent-browser-auth for browsing and agent-payer-auth for checkout and payment.
Under TAP, a request whose Signature-Input carries neither agent-browser-auth nor agent-payer-auth has not been signed by a trusted agent.
TAP defines the nonce as a session identifier: multiple message signatures in one header should share it, and each signed body object repeats the nonce of the message signature.
TAP requires the created and expires timestamps to be no more than 8 minutes apart.
The TAP specification's header examples use alg="Ed25519" for the message signature.
The TAP specification's body object examples use alg "PS256".
The TAP specification allows an agent or payment scheme to add signature fields beyond the required minimum.
The TAP consumer recognition object, agenticConsumer, contains at least nonce, idToken, contextualData, kid, alg and signature.
TAP's contextualData object contains countryCode, zip, ipAddress and deviceData.
In TAP, ipAddress and deviceData describe the consumer's device as collected during the Payment Instruction.
The TAP ID Token is a JWT per RFC 7519 that is compatible with an OpenID Connect ID Token and is signed by Visa as a JWS.
The TAP ID Token header requires alg, kid and typ, with typ JWT+ext.id_token and the none algorithm not supported.
The TAP specification prefers PS256 to RS256 for the ID Token signature.
The TAP ID Token carries the public claims iss, sub, aud, exp and iat, and optionally jti, auth_time and amr.
The TAP ID Token can carry obfuscated phone_number and email claims with their verified flags, plus phone_number_mask and email_mask for display.
Because no identity arrives in the clear, a merchant using the Visa ID Token must keep a table that maps obfuscated phone numbers or emails to its own account holders.
The TAP payment container, agenticPaymentContainer, contains at least nonce, kid, alg and signature.
A TAP payment container can also carry paymentCredentialsHash, cardMetadata, an encrypted payload or a browsingIOU, depending on how the merchant processes payment.
TAP's cardMetadata object includes lastFour, paymentAccountReference and shortDescription, plus card art data.
TAP's payment credential hash covers the 16-digit account number, expiry month, expiry year and 3-digit security code, and is used for key-entered guest checkout.
The TAP specification says a merchant should decline when its own hash of the key-entered card data does not match the payment credential hash.

TAP's encrypted payload is encrypted with the merchant's public key and holds a Token object (paymentToken, expirationMonth, expirationYear, cardholderName), dynamicData, ShippingAddress and BillingAddress objects, and consumerEmailAddress, consumerName and consumerMobileNumber.
TAP's browsingIOU contains invoiceId, amount, cardAcceptorId, acquirerId, uri, sequenceCounter, paymentService, kid, alg and signature.
TAP's browsingIOU is present when a merchant has asked for payment with an HTTP 402 response.
TAP publishes no JSON Schema, OpenAPI file or test vectors for its objects.
The TAP sample repository does not implement the consumer recognition object or the payment container.
The TAP specification's JSON example spells the ID Token field IdToken while its field table says idToken.
The TAP specification names the credential hash paymentCredentialsHash in its example and credentialHash in its processing section.
The first TAP header example spells the key parameter keyId, while the field table and later examples use keyid.

Until at least 2026-10-10 the TAP specification named https://mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks as the well-known location of Visa's public keys; the page Visa moved to developer.visa.com/docs (read 2026-10-19) says Visa publishes its keys at a well-known location but names no URL.
The TAP specification also describes a key retrieval operation as GET /keys with a keyID parameter returning a JWK with kty, kid, use, alg, n and e.
On 2026-10-11 and again on 2026-10-19, https://mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks returned a JWK Set with one 2048-bit RSA key and no Ed25519 key.

On 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19, the single key at https://mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks had no alg or use member and carried a certificate for vic-oauth-jwe.visa.com issued by a Visa sandbox issuing CA.
Visa's well-known JWKS was served with cache-control public, max-age=3600 on 2026-10-11.

Visa has not published how production TAP agent keys reach verifiers: as read on 2026-10-19, the specification names no key URL and gives its GET /keys operation no host, and Visa's API reference lists a Visa Agent Registry Services entry open only to authorized users.
A TAP verifier checks, in order, that a TAP tag is present, that all minimum fields are present, the time window, the nonce, the public key and the signature.
Under TAP, a missing minimum field, a bad time window, a reused nonce, a missing or expired key, or a failed signature each lead to blocking the request.
TAP's nonce check applies only if the verifier keeps a record of nonces received in the last 8 minutes.
A TAP consumer recognition object or payment container is signed with the same private key as the message signature and carries the same nonce.
The signature base for TAP body objects is all fields in the order received except the signature, with no named canonicalization.
TAP lets a merchant use consumer recognition data even when its verification fails.
TAP says payment container data should not be used for payment when required fields are missing, the nonce does not match or the signature fails.
TAP allows the payment container nonce check to be skipped when a payment is required without a message signature.
With a browsingIOU, the merchant checks the IOU against its 402 response and the signature, then grants access expecting funds at settlement.

The TAP merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) defines neither the format of the HTTP 402 response nor how a browsingIOU is settled; it only lists the IOU fields taken from the 402 (invoiceId, amount, cardAcceptorId).
Cloudflare's published TAP checks are: headers present, key fetched by keyid, time window, nonce uniqueness, valid tag, signature base rebuilt, and Ed25519 verification.
Cloudflare's 2025-10-24 post shows an example request with tag web-bot-auth even though its listed checks require agent-browser-auth or agent-payer-auth.
Visa's TAP overview page, retired in October 2026, said agents generate TAP signatures following the Visa Intelligent Commerce Client Implementation Guide for onboarded agents, which is not public.
The TAP sample CDN proxy requires signatures only on paths starting with /product/ and forwards other paths without verification.

TAP defines no lifecycle objects of its own (no order, mandate or token). The state it relies on sits with the parties: the verifier's optional nonce record and key cache, the merchant's record of the 402 data it issued, the merchant's mapping table from obfuscated phone or email values to its accounts, and the agent's IOU sequence counter.
TAP places its two signed objects in the HTTP request body and its agent signature in HTTP headers.
The TAP repository README says merchants receive identifiers via query parameters, while the specification places the signed objects in the request body.
The TAP specification says agents can communicate over web or API channels and protocols such as MCP and ACP, but it publishes no binding for them.
RFC 9421, HTTP Message Signatures, is a Standards Track RFC dated February 2024.
RFC 9530, Digest Fields, is a Standards Track RFC dated February 2024 that obsoletes RFC 3230.
TAP's required signature components include no Content-Digest, so unless an agent or scheme adds one, the TAP message signature does not cover the request body.

RFC 9421 requires alg values to come from the HTTP Signature Algorithms registry, whose initial entries are rsa-pss-sha512, rsa-v1_5-sha256, hmac-sha256, ecdsa-p256-sha256, ecdsa-p384-sha384 and ed25519.
The TAP sample code uses the alg value rsa-pss-sha256, which is not in RFC 9421's initial algorithm registry.
The TAP sample agent and CDN proxy serialize signature parameters with a space after each semicolon, unlike RFC 9421's structured field serialization.
The TAP sample merchant backend builds a signature base with nonce, created and expires lines and no @signature-params line, which does not follow RFC 9421.
The TAP sample CDN proxy does not check the tag value or the 8-minute window, keeps nonces for one hour and caches keys for 5 milliseconds.
The TAP sample agent sets expires to created plus 8 minutes and uses a random UUID as the nonce.
The TAP sample agent registry accepts agent and key registrations without authentication.
The TAP specification's Python sample writes the @authority and @path component names without quotes, unlike RFC 9421.
The IETF Web Bot Auth working group draft draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 was posted on 2026-09-01 and is still the current revision on 2026-10-11.
The authors of draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 are T. Meunier of Cloudflare and S. Major of Google.
TAP launched almost eleven months before the Web Bot Auth working group draft -00, so that draft is not the basis of TAP.
The TAP specification says its agent recognition signature is based on RFC 9421 and aligned with web-bot-auth.
TAP does not conform to the Web Bot Auth working group draft: the draft requires tag web-bot-auth while TAP uses agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft requires a Signature-Agent header that the signature covers; TAP's required fields include no Signature-Agent.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft requires keyid to be a base64url JWK SHA-256 thumbprint; TAP treats keyid as a key identifier without that rule.
TAP requires a nonce, while the Web Bot Auth working group draft adds no nonce requirement beyond RFC 9421.

The Web Bot Auth working group draft finds keys through a Signature-Agent URL, by default a directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory on that origin, or a JWK Set URI or client metadata document; TAP looks keys up by keyid in the payment scheme's key store, at a well-known URL that its specification named until at least 2026-10-10 and no longer names.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft recommends an expiry of no more than 24 hours, while TAP allows at most 8 minutes.

The example keyid, nonce, timestamps and Signature value in the TAP specification are the same values as a test vector in the Web Bot Auth working group draft that signs a different base with tag web-bot-auth.
The TAP specification's own example has created and expires 3,600 seconds apart, which breaks its 8-minute rule.
The TAP specification shows the same Signature value for its browsing and checkout examples although their tags differ, so the examples cannot both verify.
TAP's minimum covered components do not include @method, the query string or a content digest.
The TAP merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) states no algorithm or salt for the payment credential hash.
The GitHub security advisories list for visa/trusted-agent-protocol was empty on 2026-10-11 and on 2026-10-19.

On 2026-10-19 an NVD keyword search for 'Trusted Agent Protocol' found no CVE about Visa's TAP (its one hit, CVE-2026-100567, is unrelated), and neither the repository's GitHub advisory list nor a GitHub Advisory Database search named TAP.
The formal analysis in arXiv 2609.00060 models x402, MPP, ACP and AP2 and does not model TAP.
Visa says TAP integrates continuous telemetry into Visa's fraud and risk models.
Cloudflare said on 2025-10-24 that Visa and Mastercard would each host their own directory for agents registered with them.
TAP natively provides agent identity verification through RFC 9421 signatures with keys from the payment scheme's key store.

Agents register for TAP by onboarding to Visa Intelligent Commerce. Visa's rules require an Agentic Payment Provider to enroll in VIC and register with Visa, directly or through an Agentic Payment Enabler; neither the rules nor the TAP specification describes the onboarding or key-registration steps (checked 2026-10-19).
TAP natively limits a signature's lifetime to 8 minutes through created and expires.
TAP's replay protection is partial because nonce tracking is optional for the verifier.
The TAP merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) defines no revocation list or key status endpoint; a key that cannot be retrieved or has expired means the message should be blocked.
Spending limits, consent capture and step-up authentication sit in Visa Intelligent Commerce, not in TAP.

TAP defines no receipt. Visa's VIC developer page said (archived 2026-10-03) that VIC collects commerce signals that allow quick resolution of most disputes; its workflows page (2026-10-19) says Visa retains the agent's post-purchase confirmation data for disputes.
The TAP merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) defines no reputation mechanism for agents.
TAP is off-chain; its merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) defines no events, explorers or indexers.
No public count of merchants that verify TAP signatures had been published as of 2026-10-11.
Cloudflare exposes a cf.bot_management.signed_agent field for Web Bot Auth agents, which requires an Enterprise plan with Bot Management.
Since 2026-07-01 Cloudflare treats signed agents as verified bots, distinguished by a Direct versus Intermediary access field.
TAP's consumer recognition object sends the consumer's IP address, device data, country code and postal code to the merchant.
The TAP merchant specification (read 2026-10-19) gives no data minimization or retention rule for consumer recognition data.
Visa says every Agentic Ready transaction in Europe was secured with Visa Payment Passkeys, supporting compliance with Strong Customer Authentication.
Visa says Intelligent Commerce Connect can handle orchestration and PCI compliance for enablers processing agentic transactions for merchants.

In VIC, enrolling a card provisions an agent-specific token through the Visa Token Service, followed by issuer step-up verification where required and Visa Payment Passkey setup with device binding; credentials can be retrieved only after that, unless Visa has approved the use case to skip the passkey.
In VIC the consumer authenticates each purchase instruction, with a Visa Payment Passkey or another issuer-approved method, before the agent can retrieve payment credentials.

Visa's VIC API client in the visa/ai repository calls POST /vacp/v1/instructions, PUT /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}, PUT /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/cancel, POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/credentials and POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/confirmations.
Visa's VIC API client enrolls cards with POST /vacp/v1/cards.

Visa's VIC developer page said (archived 2026-10-03) that payments would initially use guest checkout with key entry (form fill); its workflows page (2026-10-19) has the agent submit the credential to the merchant checkout or a PSP-enabled flow.
The GitHub repository visa/mcp now resolves to visa/ai, created 2025-11-05 under the MIT license.
The visa/ai repository contains workspace packages @visa/token-manager, @visa/mcp-client and @visa/api-client, which are not published on npm.
Visa's MCP examples use the sandbox base URL https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com.
Visa announced its MCP server for Visa Intelligent Commerce and a pilot of the Visa Acceptance Agent Toolkit on 2025-09-04.
The visa/vic-reference-agent repository, created 2026-01-23, carries a proprietary VIC Reference Agent License Agreement limited to evaluation with test data.
GitHub describes visa/vic-reference-agent as an open source reference app although its license is proprietary.
Akamai and Visa announced on 2025-12-17 that TAP is supported across Akamai Cloud.
Visa's 2026-07-02 release says Cloudflare and Akamai support TAP implementation at the infrastructure level.
Cloudflare said on 2025-10-24 that it would bring TAP support to its Agents SDK and create managed rules to allow registered agents.
Visa unveiled Intelligent Commerce Connect on 2026-04-08 as a pilot that lets merchants accept agent payments initiated through TAP, MPP, ACP and UCP.
Visa's 2026-04-08 release names Aldar, AWS, Diddo, Highnote, Mesh, Payabli and Sumvin as Intelligent Commerce Connect pilot partners.
Visa announced the Agentic Directory and Agent Score on 2026-06-10 at Visa Payments Forum.
Visa describes the Agentic Directory as including agents and merchants that Visa has verified as legitimate participants in agentic commerce.
Visa's Agent Score, created with New Generation, lets merchants evaluate whether AI agents can navigate and complete tasks on their websites.
Visa's 2026-07-02 release says merchant participation in live European agent purchases was enabled through TAP and the Agent Directory.
Visa names lastminute.com, Frasers, Cleverbridge and BrickDepot as merchants in its live European agentic transactions.
eDreams ODIGEO announced on 2026-07-03 that it uses Visa's TAP and Agentic Directory to recognize verified AI agents on its eDreams, Opodo, GO Voyages and Travellink brands.
The mppx SDK includes a TAP attestation profile with tags agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth and a default and maximum lifetime of 480 seconds.
Tempo's MPP blog announced TAP and Web Bot Auth request attestation in mppx on 2026-08-12.

Visa has published no standalone TAP library on npm or PyPI (checked 2026-10-19). Release candidates of Visa Crypto Labs' @visa/cli 5.0.0 (npm rc tag, from 2026-09-18) sign TAP requests; the current release, 4.0.1, does not.

Visa's developer page for Visa Intelligent Commerce said (archived 2026-10-03) that VIC is free to use in sandbox and asked businesses to contact Visa for production fees; the VIC pages that replaced it in October 2026 state no fees.
The TAP Product Terms state no license fee.
Nevermined's 2026-08-19 review says public documentation gives no universal production price for Visa Intelligent Commerce.

A Merchant Cost Consulting opinion piece of 2026-05-01 expects new agentic fee categories at the network level and points to Visa's plan to scale CLI commerce with pricing; it names no published agentic interchange rate.
Worldpay wrote on 2026-07-30 that no liability shift for agentic transactions exists yet.

Worldpay says that when an agent authenticates properly and its token is issued correctly, liability generally follows existing tokenized-transaction rules for fraud, while disputes short of fraud, such as an agent misreading an instruction, remain unsettled.

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. Since 2025-10-18 they have made the cardholder responsible, within Visa's system, for an Agentic Payment Provider's actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it. Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift; they set no agent-specific fee or interchange rate and do not mention TAP.
Visa's TAP launch release cites a rise of over 4,700% in AI-driven traffic to US retail websites over the prior year, from Adobe data of August 2025.
Visa reported a 25% increase in malicious bot-initiated transactions over six months, and a 40% increase in the US.
Visa said on 2025-12-18 that hundreds of agent-initiated transactions had been completed with partners.
Visa said on 2025-12-18 that it works with more than 100 partners on agentic commerce, with over 30 building in the VIC sandbox and over 20 agents and enablers integrating directly.
Visa's 2025-12-18 release says Visa and more than 10 partners introduced TAP in October 2025.
Akamai cited a 300% rise in AI-powered bot traffic over a year and more than 25 billion AI bot requests to commerce in two months, from its 2025 Digital Fraud and Abuse Report.
Visa launched the Agentic Ready programme in Europe on 2026-03-17 with 21 named early issuing partners.
Visa expanded Agentic Ready to Asia Pacific and Latin America on 2026-04-29, saying it was live with more than 20 partners in the UK and Europe and would roll out to 85 or more partners.
Visa's 2026-07-02 release names 31 European issuers that completed live agent-executed transactions at participating merchants.
Visa's live European agent transactions announced on 2026-07-02 took place at merchant websites rather than controlled test storefronts.
Visa published a card specification and the mpp-card SDK for the Machine Payments Protocol on 2026-03-18.
Visa's 2026-03-18 post says its MPP card spec and SDK are built on Visa Intelligent Commerce and the Trusted Agent Protocol.
The npm package mpp-card was created on 2026-03-12 and reached version 0.1.8 on 2026-03-18, under Visa's own terms rather than an open source license.
The MPP card method draft draft-card-charge-00 is authored by Jacob Brans of Visa.
draft-card-charge-00 says a client may include Trusted Agent Protocol signature headers for additional identity assurance, so TAP is optional in the MPP card flow.

The sentence making TAP headers optional has been in draft-card-charge-00 since Visa's Jacob Brans added the file (PR #169, merged 2026-03-14; public in the repository's init commit on 2026-03-18), and was still there at the 2026-10-16 repository head.
Visa is a Premier member of the x402 Foundation according to the Linux Foundation's 2026-07-14 announcement.
Visa's TAP launch release says Visa is collaborating with Coinbase to align on interoperability with x402.
TAP's browsingIOU answers an HTTP 402 with card acquiring data and does not use x402's headers or payloads.

The TAP sample merchant returns HTTP 402 with an ad hoc JSON body and ad hoc X-Payment-* headers (X-Payment-Required, X-Payment-Amount and others) that its comments call x402 headers, rather than the x402 wire format.
Visa's launch release says Visa is working with partners so that TAP will complement the Agentic Commerce Protocol.
Neither the TAP merchant specification nor the Agentic Commerce Protocol repository (main at 7fdd78d, searched 2026-10-19) defines a binding between TAP and ACP.
UCP specifies its own RFC 9421 request signing with Content-Digest and keys published in /.well-known/ucp, plus an optional Web Bot Auth profile with Signature-Agent and tag web-bot-auth.
UCP's request signing is closer to the IETF Web Bot Auth draft than TAP is, and the UCP specification does not mention TAP.
Visa is listed as an endorser on ucp.dev.
The AP2 repository does not mention Visa or the Trusted Agent Protocol.
Visa co-chairs the FIDO Alliance Payments Working Group, launched 2025-04-29, and Google contributed AP2 to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28.
Cloudflare says Visa's TAP and Mastercard's Agent Pay both build on Web Bot Auth by adding a tag for browsing or purchasing and requiring a nonce.
Stripe added support for Visa Intelligent Commerce and Mastercard Agent Pay agentic network tokens to its Shared Payment Tokens on 2026-03-03.

Visa calls its agent credentials agentic network tokens, agent-specific tokens or agentic tokens, while Mastercard Agentic Tokens are Mastercard's Agent Pay credentials; they are different products on different networks.
Neither the TAP merchant specification and the visa/trusted-agent-protocol repository (commit 16d59bd) nor the ERC-8004 text and contracts repository mentions the other (searched 2026-10-19).

Visa calls TAP an open framework, but its specification and sample code are under revocable terms that bar modifying the specification and allow sample-code changes only inside conforming applications.
The TAP specification misspells RFC 9421 as RCF 9421.

The TAP specification names a shared key approach across payment schemes as a goal. For now Visa runs its own key store; Cloudflare said in October 2025 that Visa and Mastercard would each host a directory, and the only Mastercard directory host in its guide did not resolve on 2026-10-19.
Open issues in the TAP repository ask what standing a payment instruction has after its agent is revoked and how to sign transaction receipts.
The arXiv paper 2606.08790, RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce, names Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol in its text.
arXiv 2501.09674 is Authenticated Delegation and Authorized AI Agents by Tobin South and others, first posted 2025-01-16.
arXiv 2609.27452, Issuer-Sovereign Agentic Payments, first posted 2026-09-23, argues for keeping agent spending controls with the issuing bank.
Murdoch and Anderson analyzed Verified by Visa and MasterCard SecureCode at Financial Cryptography 2010.
Privacy Pass: Bypassing Internet Challenges Anonymously appeared in Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies in 2018.

Visa's Jacob Brans added draft-card-charge-00 in PR #169, merged on 2026-03-14 while the mpp-specs repository was private; it became public in the repository's init commit on 2026-03-18, and the optional TAP sentence is in it from the start.
The mppx TAP verifier checks the signature, the request authority and path, the signature lifetime, the intent tag and the nonce.
Mppx.create answers an invalid request attestation with HTTP 401 and an absent attestation or unresolved key with HTTP 403.
The MPP documentation says a request attestation does not authorize a payment or prove the end user's identity.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft requires the signature to cover @authority or @target-uri and recommends adding components such as @method, @path and @query-param to narrow its scope.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft warns that a signature covering only the authority can be reused for any method, path or body until it expires.
The Web Bot Auth working group draft serves its key directory with the media type application/http-message-signatures-directory+json.
When the key for a payment container cannot be located, the TAP specification says only that the content may be inaccurate, while its other payment checks say the data should not be used for payment.
Mastercard's Level 1 guide says Agent Pay agents use the single tag value Agent-pay-auth, while agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth are Visa's tags.

The only Mastercard key directory host in Mastercard's Level 1 guide, agentpay-key-directory.mastercard.com, did not resolve in DNS on 2026-10-11 or 2026-10-19, and Cloudflare's post names no Mastercard directory, so neither source gives a working location.
The TAP sample CDN proxy records a nonce before it verifies the signature and has its rate limiting commented out.

The TAP specification lists four benefits of its agent signature: strong identity tied to a payment scheme program, tamper-proof requests, replay protection through timestamps and nonces, and no reliance on IP addresses or extra header content.
The TAP specification says a public key associated with Visa implies that the agent takes part in, and complies with, the Visa Intelligent Commerce program requirements.
Visa's TAP overview page, retired in October 2026, described three kinds of verifiable information: agent intent, consumer recognition and payment information.
The TAP specification's benefits text says the signature covers critical parts of the message such as method, path and headers, but its required minimum covers only @authority and @path.

TAP's trust model has three signatures: an agent recognition signature in the message header, a signed consumer or device identity in the request body, and a signed payment container in the request body.
Under TAP the consumer recognition object is provided while browsing and may be provided at payment, while the payment container comes at payment or whenever the merchant requests a payment.
The TAP payment container section also leaves it to the merchant's discretion whether the object's content is usable when verification fails.
The TAP specification's Python sample builds a @signature-params line that starts with the label sig2= and leaves out the alg parameter, unlike its header examples and RFC 9421.
Under TAP, a merchant that wants the encrypted payment payload onboards its public key to each payment scheme it accepts through a scheme-specific API.

Until October 2026 Visa's TAP overview page listed a consumer's blockchain wallet address among the consumer recognition data an agent may pass, which the specification's object tables do not define; Visa's current TAP pages no longer mention it.
The TAP specification targets agents that are initially unknown to the merchant, and merchants that have not adopted it can ignore its signatures.
The TAP specification says a merchant that recognizes agents may present an agent-specific experience, such as simpler pages or fewer checkout steps.
Under TAP, the keys at Visa's well-known URL verify the message signature, the ID Token JWS and the signed body objects.

Visa's TAP overview page, retired in October 2026, said merchants and their proxies, such as CDNs and bot mitigation services, have historically classed automated web traffic as bots and typically blocked it.

The TAP specification defines two interactions: browsing, to learn product details, availability and the final cost after taxes and shipping, and payment, to buy a product or gain paid access to a resource.

Visa's rules require an issuer to pay for an Agentic Transaction processed under a cardholder's payment instructions and not to block Agentic Payment Provider transactions wholesale. For disputes processed from 2026-10-24, an Agentic Payment Provider's login ID counts among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute.

Visa's own token manager in the visa/ai repository fetches the JWKS at its MCP base URL's /.well-known/jwks and uses that RSA key's certificate to encrypt JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP-256) for Visa's MCP server.

Between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-19 Visa moved its TAP pages to developer.visa.com/docs/trusted-agent-protocol: the specification and Product Terms moved, the overview page was retired, and the moved specification no longer names a key URL.

As seen on 2026-10-19, Visa's API reference lists a Trusted Agent Protocol entry labeled v1 with one sandbox endpoint, GET /v1/trustedAgentProtocol, and no schemas; the specification itself carries no version.
A ChainIT white paper posted to arXiv on 2026-10-16 (2610.22899) names Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol in its related work.
The mppx SDK gained TAP request attestation in wevm/mppx PR #732, merged on 2026-08-04, and first shipped it in mppx 0.8.17 on 2026-08-10.
EMVCo's draft framework for card-based agentic payments, released for feedback on 2026-09-01, did not name TAP when read on 2026-10-11.

In Visa's VIC API examples the consumer authenticates the purchase instruction first, and the client sends that verification result (assuranceData) inside the POST /vacp/v1/instructions request, to the sandbox REST host sandbox.api.visa.com.
